LESSON: WRITING 10.4.1 CREATIVE WRITING

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 10
Topic 10.4: Writing 10.4.1 Creative Writing
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 10.4.1 Creative Writing, part of Strand 10 in Grade 4 ENGLISH LANGUAGE.

Key inquiry question: Why should you organise your thoughts in clear sentences and paragraphs? 2. How can you tell others about yourself?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. describe the parts of a descriptive composition for self-expression,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 10.4.1 Creative Writing in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. organise thoughts clearly, precisely and creatively into a coherent paragraph for self- expression,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 10.4.1 Creative Writing in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. create a descriptive composition of about 80- 100 words on various topics for effective communication,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 10.4.1 Creative Writing in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. promote the role of creativity in descriptive writing for effective communication.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 10.4.1 Creative Writing in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. read a sample descriptive composition of about 80-100 words with peers and identify the paragraphs,
2. talk about different activities they engage in such as ‘

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 10.4.1 Creative Writing together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Self-efficacy: This is achieved as the learner writes descriptive compositions for effective communication.

• Learning to learn: It is enhanced as the learner works with peers to discover how to write descriptive compositions.

Values:
• Responsibility: This is nurtured as the learner engages in assigned roles and duties in different activities of planning and

writing a descriptive composition.

• Unity: It is achieved as the learner shares the available resources like the digital devices so that peers can as well type

their descriptive compositions on the device.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Proper Sanitation: This is achieved as the learner talks about ‘how to clean a house’ before peers making them learn

sanitation from each other.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner relates the skill of descriptive writing to writing skills taught in Kiswahili.

3. create a descriptive composition of about 80- 100 words on various topics for effective communication,
4. promote the role of creativity in descriptive writing for effective communication.
